penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Interview kits, rubrics, and assessment frameworks require domain-expert authorship and iterative customization per company's engineering culture — this is content consulting work, not automated delivery.

rationale: Engineering hiring managers at 20–500 person companies are a sharp, nameable buyer with real budget (HackerRank charges $25k+/yr, Karat charges per interview). The pain is current and well-articulated — the AI-era interview format gap is a live problem in Nov 2026. However, delivering genuinely useful, company-specific interview kits requires expert customization that cannot be fully automated: each company has different engineering culture, tech stack, and AI-use norms. The requires_human_fulfillment penalty reflects that the actual deliverable (a defensible, calibrated interview rubric) needs expert human input per client, pushing the total to 4.6 — below validate.
solution_plan: Not recommended as currently conceived. If repositioned as a self-serve document generator (buyer inputs their stack/role/AI policy and gets a template kit instantly, no customization), the human-fulfillment penalty would not apply. That version: (1) A Claude-powered interview kit generator — input your role, stack, and AI stance; get a structured interview guide with questions, rubric, and scoring sheet. (2) Build: a simple intake form + Claude prompt chain + PDF/Markdown output + Stripe payment link ($49–$99 per kit). (3) Sell: outreach to engineering managers on LinkedIn, referencing the HN thread directly — Youval approves each batch. (4) Maintain: fully automated once a buyer pays. The repositioned version would score meaningfully higher on operational_autonomy; operator should re-submit as a revised opportunity if they want that scored.
notes: Total 4.6 drops below validate threshold primarily due to human-fulfillment penalty. Repositioning as self-serve template generator (not customized consulting) would change the score significantly.
